items.detail: Model::turn takes one request, a caller-owned sink and a cancellation token, and makes one attempt: bounded text and tool items, streamed events, typed failures with independent dispatch evidence, and opaque state bound to its protocol, provider, account, endpoint, model and binding revision.
items.label: A neutral model turn

items.detail: The start of a streamed tool call names the tool before any argument fragment, in all three protocol projections.
items.label: Streamed tool calls carry their announced name

items.detail: Reasoning state that arrives in a client request is held unattributed, and every egress path refuses it until the caller binds it to a target of the same protocol.
items.label: Opaque state from ingress cannot be sent until bound

items.detail: Error::retriable and Error::may_retry: the transport marks 408, 429 (a 429 a client's quota rule reads as an exhausted quota excepted), 5xx, no response, a body failing mid-stream and a stream ending inside an event; unauthorized, refused, invalid and cancelled failures never are. An error status carrying x-should-retry: false is final whatever its status.
items.label: Every failure says whether it may be retried

items.detail: TurnRequest.controls carries a thinking mode, the parallel-tool-call choice and advisory hints (prompt cache, cache key, verbosity, reasoning summary, unforwarded field names); wire_effort is the one reasoning table (max reaches Chat Completions and Responses as xhigh), and a turn with controls is llm.turn/4.
items.label: Thinking, parallel tool calls and advisory hints in the neutral turn

items.detail: docs/contract-v1.md states turn ownership, validation, accounting, pricing, credentials and compatibility; the versioned envelopes (llm.turn/3 and /4, llm.outcome/4, llm.usage/2, llm.cost/2, llm.binding/1, llm.catalog/1) refuse unknown versions and fields.
items.label: A written contract and compatibility policy

items.detail: Capabilities carries output_streaming and input_during_output; every client here declares true and false, a document written before them keeps its binding revision and configuration digest, and a binding, catalog or route claiming input during output or unstreamed output is refused.
items.label: A model declares whether its output streams and whether input can reach a running turn

items.detail: One attempt per call, explicit deadlines, no redirects, no ambient proxy, bounded bodies, and partial output kept when a stream fails.
items.label: Bounded HTTP and server-sent events

items.detail: A 15-second connect timeout (HttpClient::with_connect_timeout), a 180-second idle bound by default, and cancellation that wins over a pending read.
items.label: Connect and idle bounds, and cancellation

items.detail: The transport and providers joined the other domains in 0.1.3; the conformance runner answers at least 937 scenarios against the real crates three times and skips none.
items.label: Every library crate is specified in ESS

items.detail: ChatClient and an ingress codec for any compatible endpoint, including an anonymous local vLLM server or llama.cpp llama-server; usage is always requested on a stream, and llama-server's timings counters are read beside it.
items.label: Chat Completions projection and client

items.detail: MessagesClient and an ingress codec; signed and redacted thinking cross as bound opaque state.
items.label: Messages projection and client

items.detail: Cache breakpoints on the standing instruction and on the conversation tail; an unknown stream event, delta or content block is kept as an opaque item with a warning.
items.label: Messages prompt caching and unknown events

items.detail: Request bodies and stream decoding for the declared subset, stateless (store: false) and always streamed.
items.label: Responses projection

items.detail: ResponsesClient implements Model over one Responses endpoint: the request is checked against its binding and bounded before the credential is resolved.
items.label: Responses client

items.detail: Each event reaches the caller as it arrives, and the turn carries the text the caller was shown: kept when the terminal output omits it, and kept over a server's own message whose text differs, with a shown-text-kept warning; text it cannot tie to one message overwrites none, with a shown-text-unpaired warning.
items.label: Live Responses streaming

items.detail: No event retracts or replaces one already emitted; a successful turn's assistant text is exactly the text deltas shown for it, on Responses, Messages and Chat Completions, and Responses says when it is not.
items.label: Streamed text is final

items.detail: encode_request gives the exact bytes the client sends; opt-in conversation identity sends prompt_cache_key, session-id and x-client-request-id.
items.label: Responses request encoding and conversation identity

items.detail: encode_ingress_response and IngressStream encode neutral events and an outcome as the Responses event payloads and response object this crate's decoder reads back as the same turn; partial usage and the error's message are never relayed.
items.label: A server answers a Responses caller

items.detail: encode_ingress_message and IngressStream encode the Messages event stream and message, each block, reason and usage report checked against this crate's decoder; without_reasoning_relay for an upstream that cannot sign reasoning.
items.label: A server answers a Messages caller

items.detail: Ingress carries thinking, a system of text blocks, cache_control as the prompt-cache hint, effort max and disable_parallel_tool_use; metadata is reported, never sent; everything else is refused by its path. Checked against llm-gateway's authored fixture, not a captured session.
items.label: Claude Code's first turn under written Messages rules

items.detail: Ingress carries instructions, parallel_tool_calls, prompt_cache_key, text.verbosity and reasoning.summary, reads a plain-string tool result, reports item ids and client_metadata as unsent, and refuses every unknown key at every level by its path and hosted tools by type. Checked against requests captured from Codex 0.160.0 at a loopback recorder; no provider was called.
items.label: Codex's requests under written Responses rules

items.detail: Every unknown key below the top is refused by its path, strict schemas are refused, and parallel_tool_calls, prompt_cache_key and verbosity are carried both ways.
items.label: Chat ingress closed at every level

items.detail: Chat ingress reads its own failure object as failed: true; a call rejected before it ran is sent as failed: true with the caller's reason in output, on every wire, because none carries a rejected state.
items.label: A failed tool result reads back as failed, and a rejected call has one encoding

items.detail: Each decodes on its own wire and projects onto the other two with every field under a written rule; each projection lists the advisory hints it omits, and each client warns advisory-omitted after a successful turn.
items.label: A Claude Code and a Codex first turn cross wires

items.detail: A success without a content type is read as an event stream when one was asked for, and an empty terminal output after streamed items keeps the streamed items.
items.label: Responses turns against the Codex backend

items.detail: A Responses server_error or rate_limit_exceeded and a Messages overloaded_error or api_error stream error may be retried before any output and are final after it, the rule Responses server_is_overloaded already followed; an exhausted quota stays final inside a stream and, since story:quota-429-is-final, as an HTTP 429 before it (Responses by error.code, or by error.type for insufficient_quota and the Codex backend's usage_limit_reached and usage_not_included; Messages a rate_limit_error whose error.details.error_code is enforced_spend_limit_reached). A failure an llm gateway relays inside a stream with nothing streamed first still reads back retriable; a failure before output, the gateway's HTTP 502, reads final when it carries x-should-retry: false, which llm-gateway has to send.
items.label: The provider failures Harness retried are retriable before output

items.detail: llm-bedrock signs each request with a signer written on ring, checked against the AWS test suite vendored from aws-c-auth (header signing only); keys come from StaticCredentials through an injected resolver or from ContainerCredentials at the container credentials endpoint. No AWS SDK crate and no aws-lc is a dependency. EKS Pod Identity is described from AWS documentation and unverified.
items.label: Bedrock requests are signed with Signature Version 4

items.detail: llm_bedrock::eventstream decodes frames incrementally across reads, at most 16 MiB per frame; checked against the smithy-rs vectors and recorded Bedrock bodies.
items.label: AWS event-stream frames decode, bounded

items.detail: BedrockClient with Api::Converse sends /converse-stream or /converse and reads text, tool calls, thinking and usage; the body carries no cachePoint, so an absent cache counter is a known 0 and the input total is known whenever inputTokens is. Fixture evidence only; no live Bedrock call was made.
items.label: A turn runs on Bedrock Converse

items.detail: Api::AnthropicInvoke sends the Messages body with anthropic_version: bedrock-2023-05-31 and reads the stream with the Messages decoder; invocation metrics fill only counters Messages usage left unreported. Fixture evidence only.
items.label: A turn runs on Anthropic models through Bedrock InvokeModel

items.detail: The llm.bedrock domain and 43 authored scenarios cover signing, frame decoding, container credentials and whole turns against loopback servers; the conformance runner answers at least 937 scenarios and skips none.
items.label: Bedrock behaviour is specified in ESS

items.detail: A catalog names an opaque SecretRef; the embedding injects the SecretResolver, resolution happens on every request, and renewal refreshes only the rejected generation.
items.label: Injected secret resolution and coordinated renewal

items.detail: Opt-in file (Linux, explicit absolute paths, strict ownership and mode checks), keychain and native-keychain features; read-only.
items.label: Protected-file and keychain adapters

items.detail: Opt-in environment (caller-named variables only) and json-pointer (an RFC 6901 pointer into a document another resolver returns).
items.label: Environment variables and JSON pointers

items.detail: Opt-in codex-auth-file: CodexAuthFile reads the access token of a Codex auth.json at an explicit absolute path on every request and refuses it once expired.
items.label: A Codex login, read-only

items.detail: Feature codex-renewal: renews inside a 15-minute margin through one non-retried request and writes only the token values back, atomically, refusing a file that changed meanwhile.
items.label: Codex login renewal, opt-in

items.detail: A login file that is not a Codex login, or whose token has no readable expiry, is refused as malformed and never falls back to another account.
items.label: A misconfigured Codex login is refused

items.detail: Feature secrets: SecretsResolver reads a route's reference as a name in one configured scope of the Secrets library's storage (v0.5.0), over its keychain backend or any SecretStorage, with refusals mapped to the existing SecretError codes.
items.label: Resolution through the Secrets library

items.detail: Provider, account, endpoint, model and serving declaration are separate choices; authentication and billing kind never follow from the protocol.
items.label: Bindings independent of protocol

items.detail: llm-providers: ProviderDescription parses llm.provider-description/1, an inference URL template filled only by a 1-48 byte [a-z0-9] instance, its wires and authentication, and a pinned control plane (OpenAPI URL and SHA-256, HTTPS server, four operation IDs), with no I/O. Runpod's ships as descriptions::runpod(). Fixture evidence only; no live Runpod pod or control-plane call qualifies it.
items.label: One provider description per provider

items.detail: Strict llm.catalog/1, a deterministic configuration digest, ordered opt-in selection, capability and input-token admission, and an explanation that resolves no secret.
items.label: TOML catalogs, selection and explanation

items.detail: Catalog::run_turn tries a route's declared targets in order and stops on visible output, an ineligible failure, an ambiguous dispatch, the attempt bound, the deadline, cancellation or the caller's limit.
items.label: Ordered fallback

items.detail: RetryPolicy, on by default: four attempts per target with 1, 2 and 4 second waits, server delays honoured up to 30 seconds, a turn-retried warning before each wait, then fallback.
items.label: Same-target retry before visible output

items.detail: llm-models: llm_models::routes::Routes reads llm.routes/1 (YAML endpoints with base URL, protocol and a secret reference; routes as <endpoint>/<model-id>, or direct names), expands it into an llm.catalog/1 catalog and builds RouteResolvers from env:, file: and keychain: references (features environment, file, keychain), refusing an unset variable or a missing file by the endpoint's reference before any request. Fixture evidence only.
items.label: One routes document for every consumer

items.detail: llm-models: port builds the Chat Completions, Responses or Messages client a catalog binding's protocol names, with the caller's resolver for its account, and refuses a credentialed account without one as unauthorized before any I/O; CatalogModels builds every serving model's port and is the Models ordered fallback takes.
items.label: One function builds the port a serving model declares

items.detail: API and caller-managed subscription routes with recorded live evidence. A live probe of the Codex backend found the two incompatibilities 0.1.6 fixed; no route is qualified.
items.label: OpenAI access qualified

items.detail: API and caller-managed subscription routes with recorded live evidence. The subscription presentation is built and fixture-checked: a subscription-oauth account resolves its token through its secret reference and Messages sends it as a bearer with the OAuth beta header and the client preamble; no live turn is recorded.
items.label: Anthropic access qualified

items.detail: llm-tool-call: call_tool forces one named tool on any Model and returns that call's JSON arguments or a typed ModelError; codex_model binds a Responses model to the operator's Codex login.
items.label: One forced tool call

items.detail: llm-blocking: BlockingModel runs one turn on the calling thread, hands events to a BlockingSink as they arrive, takes cancellation from any thread, and forks for concurrent turns.
items.label: A blocking adapter for a synchronous loop

items.detail: Atlas ADR 0097 decided the cutover: Harness dropped its own model wire and credential crates and builds on llm 0.8.0 since Harness commit 97ff3d7f on its main (2026-10-20); its spike had built and passed its tests on llm 0.1.7. docs/harness-parity.md cites every llm cell against 0.7.0 and lists the llm API changes the bridge meets; one needs an edit (TurnRequest.controls). Rows R28 and M27 are partial at 0.7.0, which marks fewer provider failures retriable than Harness's wires did; 0.8.0 retries those classes before any output.
items.label: Harness builds on llm

items.detail: Versioned llm.prices/1 books, exact decimal amounts, cache and compute pricing, six separate bases and unknown quantities kept unknown.
items.label: Usage pricing

items.detail: Opt-in sqlite: reservations committed before dispatch, concurrent callers serialized, uncertain charges kept across restart, and compute stop obligations.
items.label: Durable spending limits

items.detail: The gateway, hosting and provisioning crates and their ESS domains moved to their own repository, llm-gateway, in 0.2.0; llm is the client side.
items.label: Serving lives in llm-gateway

items.detail: One exact release tied to its required checks, artifacts and live provider qualification.
items.label: A qualified release

source: docs/implementation-status.md in the llm repository, at 0.10.0
